Dr. '''Robert H. Singer''' received an undergraduate degree in physical chemistry from [[Oberlin College]], and a PhD in developmental biology from [[Brandeis University]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://molbio.princeton.edu/events/event/96-Singer|title=Seminars & Events|access-date=2016-07-05|archive-date=2016-06-12|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160612161637/http://molbio.princeton.edu/events/event/96-Singer|url-status=live}}</ref> He did postdoctoral work in [[molecular biology]] at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] and the [[Weizmann Institute of Science]] in Rehovot, Israel.<ref name="RNA Article">{{cite journal|last1=Singer|first1=Robert H.|title=Reminiscences on my life with RNA: a self-indulgent perspective|journal=RNA|date=16 March 2015|volume=21|issue=4|pages=508–509|doi=10.1261/rna.050922.115|pmc=4371258|pmid=25780116}}</ref> [[Oberlin College]] granted Singer an Honorary Doctor of Science in 2016.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://new.oberlin.edu/events-activities/commencement/speakers-and-awards-2016.dot|title = Commencement 2021|date = 14 December 2017}}</ref> [[The Hebrew University of Jerusalem]] granted Singer an Honorary Doctorate in 2018.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www3.huji.ac.il/htbin/hon_doc/doc_search.pl|title=Honorary Doctorates - the Hebrew University of Jerusalem|access-date=2018-08-23|archive-date=2008-10-16|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081016123834/http://www3.huji.ac.il/htbin/hon_doc/doc_search.pl|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Academic Honors & Events |url=http://www.einstein.yu.edu/publications/inside-einstein/1/academic-honors-events |website=Albert Einstein College of Medicine |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150908005103/http://einstein.yu.edu/publications/inside-einstein/1/academic-honors-events/ |archive-date=September 8, 2015 |url-status=dead}}</ref>

Singer holds the following positions at the [[Albert Einstein College of Medicine]], New York: Professor and Co-Chair, Department of Anatomy and Structural Biology; Professor, Dominick P. Purpura Department of Neuroscience; Professor, Department of Cell Biology; Co-Director, Integrated Imaging Facility; and Co-Director, Gruss Lipper Biophotonics Center.<ref>{{cite web |title=Robert H. Singer, Ph.D. |url=http://www.einstein.yu.edu/faculty/7137/robert-singer/ |website=Albert Einstein College of Medicine |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180424035418/http://www.einstein.yu.edu/faculty/7137/robert-singer/ |archive-date=April 24, 2018 |url-status=dead}}</ref> Singer is a senior fellow at the [[Janelia Research Campus]] of the [[Howard Hughes Medical Institute]] in Virginia.<ref>{{cite web |title=Robert H. Singer, PhD |url=https://www.hhmi.org/scientists/robert-h-singer |website=Howard Hughes Medical Institute |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160527150345/https://www.hhmi.org/scientists/robert-h-singer |archive-date=May 27, 2016 |url-status=dead}}</ref>

Singer's career has been focused on the cell biology of [[RNA]], its isolation, detection, expression, and translation. A patent in situ hybridization technique his lab developed for detecting RNA in [[Morphology (biology)|morphologically]] preserved cells revealed that [[messenger RNA]] can localize in specific cellular compartments. This work has given rise to the field of RNA transport and localization, enhanced by Singer's and his colleagues’ development of imaging technology and RNA reporters. His lab has shown that the dynamics of [[RNA transcription]] on a single gene can be interrogated by live cell imaging, as well as by multiplexed fluorescent probes.

Singer's laboratories at Einstein and Janelia have been instrumental in developing rapid and sensitive microscopy that can study single molecules of RNA in living cells and in devising methods to track them through their life cycle. This technology has implications for understanding the role of RNA in such disease processes as cancer metastasis and intellectual disability. He holds 12 patents on his work.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://singerlab.org/patents|title=Patents &#124; Laboratory of Robert H. Singer, Ph.D. &#124; Albert Einstein College of Medicine|access-date=2016-07-05|archive-date=2007-08-10|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070810084513/http://singerlab.org/patents/|url-status=live}}</ref>

Singer is a member of the US [[National Academy of Sciences]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nasonline.org/news-and-multimedia/news/2013_04_30_NAS_Election.html|title=2013 NAS Members and Foreign Associates Elected|website=www.nasonline.org|access-date=2024-02-15|archive-date=2024-02-15|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240215014138/https://www.nasonline.org/news-and-multimedia/news/2013_04_30_NAS_Election.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]],<ref name="z758">{{cite journal | title=Members: ALPHABETICAL INDEX OF ACTIVE MEMBERS | journal=Bulletin of the American Academy of Arts and Sciences | publisher=American Academy of Arts & Sciences | volume=70 | issue=1 | year=2016 | issn=0002-712X | jstor=26407302 | pages=182–202 | url=https://www.amacad.org/sites/default/files/academy/multimedia/pdfs/alphalist.pdf | access-date=2024-07-12 | archive-date=2018-10-09 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181009122926/https://www.amacad.org/multimedia/pdfs/alphalist.pdf | url-status=live }}</ref> and is a Fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aaas.org/news/new-aaas-fellows-recognized-their-contributions-advancing-science|title=New AAAS Fellows Recognized for Their Contributions to Advancing Science &#124; American Association for the Advancement of Science (AAAS)|website=www.aaas.org}}</ref> In 2021, he received the [[Rosenstiel Award]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.brandeis.edu/rosenstiel/rosenstiel-award/index.html|title=Lewis S. Rosenstiel Award for Distinguished Work in Basic Medical Research|website=www.brandeis.edu|access-date=2024-02-15|archive-date=2021-05-08|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210508152546/https://www.brandeis.edu/rosenstiel/rosenstiel-award/index.html|url-status=live}}</ref>
